## Vegetarian Food Map (bookmark these)

| Place | Area | Style | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Osegye Hyang 오세계향** | Insadong | 100% vegan Korean — dumplings, stews, fried soy "chicken" | ₩12,000–16,000 |
| **Sanchon 산촌** | Insadong | Hanok Buddhist temple cuisine, vegan set menus, evening folk music | ₩30,000–40,000 |
| **Balwoo Gongyang 발우공양** | Jongno, by Jogyesa | Michelin-listed temple food; **reserve a day ahead**, lunch set is best value | ₩30,000–50,000 |
| **Veg In 베지인** | Insadong | Small vegan café, bowls and pasta | ₩12,000–18,000 |
| **Loving Hut / Plant** | Itaewon, Sinchon, Gangnam | Vegan chains/cafés if you detour | ₩12,000–20,000 |
| **Gwangjang Market** | Jongno 5-ga | Bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, hotteok | ₩4,000–8,000 |
| **Convenience stores** | Everywhere | Veggie kimbap (야채김밥), tofu, onigiri, bananas, soy milk | ₩1,500–5,000 |

**Watch out for:** kimchi and tteokbokki (fish sauce / anchovy broth), japchae (often beef), bibimbap (ground beef), doenjang-jjigae (sometimes meat), mandu (pork), and Myeong-dong street food generally. Temple-food restaurants are the safest, most delicious bet.

**Phrase card** (show your phone):
- 저는 채식주의자예요 — "I'm vegetarian"
- 고기, 생선, 해산물 안 먹어요 — "No meat, fish, or seafood"
- 액젓이나 멸치육수 없이 해주세요 — "No fish sauce or anchovy broth, please"
- 비건이에요 (if vegan) / 계란·유제품은 괜찮아요 (if lacto-ovo)
- 이거 고기 들어가나요? — "Does this contain meat?"

## Practical Notes

**Transport:** T-money works on subway, buses, and taxis. Base subway fare ~₩1,400–1,500; you'll spend roughly ₩8,000–12,000/day. Subway is bilingual and signage is excellent — Line 3 is your palace/Insadong artery, Line 4 your Myeong-dong/Seoul Station artery, Line 1 links Seoul Station–Jongno–Gwangjang.

**Closed-day logic (check your actual dates):**
- **Gyeongbokgung — closed Tuesdays** (if Day 2 is a Tuesday, run Day 2 on Day 1's slot and shift everything)
- Changdeokgung & Deoksugung — closed Mondays; Jongmyo — closed Tuesdays
- Bukchon is residential: courteous hours 10:00–17:00; quiet outside them

**Weather (early November):** ~3–13°C, dry and crisp, sunset ~17:30. Layers, a light down jacket, comfortable walking shoes (you'll do 12,000–18,000 steps a day), and a scarf for Namsan's wind.

**Book ahead:** Balwoo Gongyang (dinner), Changdeokgung Huwon tour (opens ~2 weeks out, sells out), hanbok rental (walk-in is usually fine on weekdays).

**Apps:** Kakao Map or Naver Map (Google Maps walking directions are unreliable in Korea), Subway Korea, Papago for translation.

**Rough budget per person (excluding flights):**

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Hotel, Myeong-dong, 2 nights | ₩260,000–400,000 |
| Food (vegetarian, 3 days) | ₩150,000–220,000 |
| Transport incl. airport trains | ₩30,000–40,000 |
| Attractions (palaces, tower, cable car) | ₩40,000–60,000 |
| Jjimjilbang + hanbok | ₩25,000–37,000 |
| **Total** | **~₩505,000–757,000** |

**Rain plan:** swap outdoor blocks for the National Museum of Korea (free, Line 4 Ichon), Leeum Museum (Hannam), COEX Starfield Library, or Dongdaemun Design Plaza — all indoor, all subway-connected."}

## Practical Notes

**Transport:** T-money works on subway, buses, and taxis. Base subway fare ~₩1,400–1,500; you'll spend roughly ₩8,000–12,000/day. Subway is bilingual and signage is excellent — Line 3 is your palace/Insadong artery, Line 4 your Myeong-dong/Seoul Station artery, Line 1 links Seoul Station–Jongno–Gwangjang.

**Closed-day logic (check your actual dates):**
- **Gyeongbokgung — closed Tuesdays** (if Day 2 is a Tuesday, run Day 2 on Day 1's slot and shift everything)
- Changdeokgung & Deoksugung — closed Mondays; Jongmyo — closed Tuesdays
- Bukchon is residential: courteous hours 10:00–17:00; quiet outside them

**Weather (early November):** ~3–13°C, dry and crisp, sunset ~17:30. Layers, a light down jacket, comfortable walking shoes (you'll do 12,000–18,000 steps a day), and a scarf for Namsan's wind.

**Book ahead:** Balwoo Gongyang (dinner), Changdeokgung Huwon tour (opens ~2 weeks out, sells out), hanbok rental (walk-in is usually fine on weekdays).

**Apps:** Kakao Map or Naver Map (Google Maps walking directions are unreliable in Korea), Subway Korea, Papago for translation.
